newsitem.title: USA: Senators urge Clinton to "fast-forward" fast track.
newsitem.headline: Senators urge Clinton to "fast-forward" fast track.

text.p: Four U.S. Senators urged President Bill Clinton on Wednesday to take swift action to acquire the so-called "fast track" trade negotiation authority or risk losing out on expanding economic opportunities.
Three Republicans and one Democrat said Clinton should make a strong push for Congress to act before its August recess to grant fast-track authority for the White House to negotiate trade agreements.

They said that if he delayed until September, the measure could get postponed in the end-of-session rush to pass other legislation -- and then might become bogged down in 1998 congressional election politics.
The legislation would give the administration the authority to negotiate trade deals and would give Congress a limited time to reject any resulting agreements.
The administration's expected first move would be to negotiate a free trade agreement with Chile and bring it into the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).

Calling on Clinton to "fast-forward fast track," Texas Republican Sen. Kay Bailey Hutchison said: "The United States must not be the stumbling block in efforts to widen hemispheric trade. We should be taking the lead."
Republicans tend to be more free trade-oriented than Democrats, and many Democrats are likely to want environmental and labour conditions included in trade legislation.
House Minority Leader Richard Gephardt, a Missouri Democrat who fought NAFTA, is expected to set out his opposition to fast track authority in a May 27 speech in Detroit.
But Sen. John McCain, an Arizona Republican, said Clinton had been able to get passage for NAFTA and other key trade issues and could exercise leadership on this one too.

The two other senators making the call were Bob Graham, a Florida Democrat, and Charles Grassley, an Iowa Republican. Grassley said that even in Iowa -- far from Mexico and Latin America -- farmers stood to lose out on corn sales to Chile as that nation forges free trade bonds with its neighbours.
